title: Backend entry systemdesign todo api
question: Design the REST API for a simple todo-list app: users can create accounts, and each user has their own list of todo items they can add, complete, and delete.
idealAnswer:
Lays out sensible resource-oriented routes, e.g. POST /todos, GET /todos, PATCH /todos/:id, DELETE /todos/:id, scoped to the authenticated user rather than taking a user id from the client

Chooses appropriate methods and status codes for each action (POST + 201 for create, PATCH + 200 for marking complete, DELETE + 204 for delete)

Covers authentication at a basic level, e.g. every request needs to identify the user (token or session), and the server derives which todos to return from that identity rather than trusting a user_id in the request body

Considers authorization, a user should get a 403 or 404 (not someone else's todo data) if they try to access or modify another user's todo item

Thinks about the data model: a todos table with user_id, title, completed flag, and timestamps is enough, doesn't over-engineer this simple case
